title: Trajectory Performance Map — combined model & route dashboard prototype
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Design and prototype an exploratory ‘Trajectory Performance Map’ that unifies per-model and per-route metrics into a latency/throughput/token trajectory canvas. This view is intended for SREs and Platform Engineers to quickly understand recent performance shifts, correlate traffic pattern changes with token mix, and surface regressions.

Goals: Provide a single screen to: 1) see latency and throughput trends side-by-side for a selected model OR route; 2) visualize token composition and per-token cost changes; 3) highlight anomalous windows and suggested remediation steps (e.g., throttle, route to variant).

User stories: 
- As a Platform engineer, I want to compare 99th/95th/median latency against request throughput over rolling windows so I can find tail-latency incidents tied to spikes.
- As a Product owner, I want to see token mix (prompt vs completion) and estimated per-minute cost impact so I can decide whether to change batching/quantization.
- As an SRE, I want quick filters to change environment, model family, and rollout cohorts so I can isolate whether a regression is global or tied to a deployment.

Design decisions & trade-offs: 
- Combined canvas vs separate panels: opted for a single responsive canvas with 3 sub-lanes (latency histogram + pXX breakdown, throughput timeseries, token-mode stacked area) to keep correlation in view. Trade-off: denser UI increases cognitive load — mitigated with contextual tooltips and an optional simplified snapshot mode.
- Sampling vs full fidelity: prototype uses 1s aggregated buckets for interactive testing, but backend should expose downsampled 10s/1m buckets for production to keep UI responsive.
- Anomaly signals: show lightweight rule-based flags (latency > SLO*1.4, throughput drop >20%, token-shift >15%) with ability to expand to ML-based alerts later.

Chart specs (high level): 
- Latency lane: stacked area for p50/p95/p99 with optional waterfall microtrace drill-in. Y-axis (ms) log-scale toggle. Hover shows percentile table and sample request IDs.
- Throughput lane: combined bar + line (bars = requests/min, line = concurrent requests). Secondary axis for per-second throughput.
- Token composition lane: stacked area by token role (prompt, completion, streaming overhead) with per-token-cost overlay as dotted line.
- Correlation overlay: brush selection on any lane highlights matching time windows across lanes and populates lateral incident panel.

Accessibility & responsiveness: color palettes pass WCAG contrast; patterns apply hatched textures for colorblind-safe mode. Small-screen view collapses token lane into an expandable module; desktop shows full 3-lane layout.

Open questions: 
- Do we pin the time-window to the route or to the global console time-picker? Proposal: default to global but allow route-level pin.
- Exact SLO sourcing: use route-configured SLO if present, otherwise fall back to model-profile SLO.

Next steps: iterate on annotations UX (what remediation actions to surface), run 5 cross-functional usability sessions, and hand off chart spec tokens to ENG for implementation planning.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma with interactive time-brush between lanes
Design spec includes explicit series definitions and axis behaviors for latency/throughput/tokens
Usability test notes from at least 5 users and at least 3 actionable changes incorporated
Implementation RFC created by ENG that maps backend metrics to UI series (ENG-8342)
